verdict.rationale: vLLM is a local and self-hosted inference engine, and products of this kind can plausibly offer a hosted cloud tier, so the axis applies. Nothing in the evidence shows vLLM offering a hosted cloud tier for running large models without downloading them. Quantization, distributed parallelism and the Docker image are adjacent self-hosting features, not a vendor-hosted offload capability.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can offload very large models to a hosted cloud tier without downloading them when my local hardware is insufficient
